Hi Anna / Peter —

Thanks again for the demo last week. As discussed, we'd like to kick off a focused implementation sprint to enable realtime outputs, function/tool calling, and the structured JSON schemas you need for downstream ingestion. Goals for the first 2 weeks:

- Confirm final JSON schema for live outputs (schema v0.9 attached).
- Wire function/tool calling for your Lookup & Billing APIs (idempotency + auth flow).
- Validate streaming latency SLOs for 95th percentile under your expected concurrency.

Could you share availability for a 60-minute kickoff tomorrow or Friday? Proposed agenda attached (Redwood Kickoff Agenda). Please also fill out the short onboarding questionnaire (attached) — it helps us scope any custom integrations (e.g., SAML, private VPC).

Technical owners on our side: Aditya (solutions eng) will architect the toolcall wiring and Marcus (runtime) will own streaming perf tuning. Monica (CS) will lead the success criteria and rollout plan.

Next steps after kickoff: mutual action plan with milestones, a temporary sandbox key for early tests, and a short evaluation suite.

Thanks — looking forward to kicking this off.

Best,

Hi Anna —

Quick answers ahead of the kickoff so we can use time for architecture / walk-through:

1) OAuth bearer tokens: yes, Redwood supports per-request bearer tokens. For short-lived tokens we recommend k/v cache for token exchange in the tool adapter layer; we can also support a signed token exchange flow if you prefer zero-credential storage in our sandbox. Please indicate token TTL and refresh flow in the questionnaire.

2) Structured output validation: Redwood's default policy is permissive — we return the structured payload and a validation status object. We can flip to strict validation (reject output) when you want blocking behavior. For onboarding I'd recommend permissive with regressions monitored in Redwood Console.

3) Sample traffic tooling: yes — we have a lightweight traffic-replay harness that can ingest a CSV of representative prompts and conversational context and replay them at configurable concurrency. We'll provide the harness as a script plus a small Docker image.

I'll prepare a short demo of the toolcall wiring (Lookup -> Billing) and show how the function call lifecycle appears in logs and trace. Marcus will have initial perf knobs for streaming (batch target, max latency per token, kv cache warmup).

See attached: preliminary checklist and a small sample toolcall adapter spec (inline in the doc).

Cheers,
Aditya
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
